title: Topic 11.4: Reading 11.4.1 Intensive reading: Dilemma Narratives

pages.lesson:
LESSON: READING 11.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: DILEMMA NARRATIVES

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 11
Topic 11.4: Reading 11.4.1 Intensive reading: Dilemma Narratives

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Reading 11.4.1 Intensive reading: Dilemma Narratives. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: What are the qualities of a good narrator?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. describe the characters in a given dilemma narrative
2. recognise a closing formula as a feature of dilemma narratives

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. describe the characters in a given dilemma narrative
   In simple words: practise until you can describe the characters in a given dilemma narrative. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

2. recognise a closing formula as a feature of dilemma narratives
   In simple words: practise until you can recognise a closing formula as a feature of dilemma narratives. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Reading 11.4.1 Intensive reading: Dilemma Narratives using something you see at school in Kenya.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county, estate, or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Underline two new ideas about Reading 11.4.1 Intensive reading: Dilemma Narratives in the examples.
2. Explain Reading 11.4.1 Intensive reading: Dilemma Narratives to a parent using one local example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Reading 11.4.1 Intensive reading: Dilemma Narratives.
4. Show that you can: describe the characters in a given dilemma narrative

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading 11.4.1 Intensive reading: Dilemma Narratives using examples from school or home.
2. Answer: Why is Reading 11.4.1 Intensive reading: Dilemma Narratives important for a Grade 7 learner?
3. Make a one-minute oral presentation to a parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Read the dilemma narrative in a given text and describe the characters,
2. Identify a closing formula as a feature of dilemma narratives,
3. Discuss what makes dilemma narratives interesting,
4. Draw a chart showing the sequence of events in a dilemma narrative,

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What are the qualities of a good narrator?
2. How can narratives contribute to decision making?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. describe the characters in a given dilemma narrative
2. recognise a closing formula as a feature of dilemma narratives

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
